query: Refactor LLM pipeline stage prompts to keep main agent context low via ephemeral spawn-delegate-die subagents
sub_questions: What proven patterns keep orchestrator main agent context window low in multi-agent LLM pipelines?
How do ephemeral spawn-delegate-die subagents work in Claude Code OpenCode and similar harnesses?
What are best practices for splitting large prompt files into lean orchestrator prompts plus detailed worker prompts?
How to enforce disjoint file ownership and safe integration when parallel subagents edit code?
What verification patterns avoid repeated full test coverage gates while keeping per-file guarantees?

findings.sub_question: What proven patterns keep orchestrator main agent context window low in multi-agent LLM pipelines?
findings.claim: Give each subagent its own context window so it explores in parallel and returns only condensed findings to the lead agent.
findings.quote: Subagents facilitate compression by operating in parallel with their own context windows, exploring different aspects of the question simultaneously before condensing the most important tokens for the lead research agent.
findings.title: How we built our multi-agent research system | Anthropic

findings.sub_question: What proven patterns keep orchestrator main agent context window low in multi-agent LLM pipelines?
findings.claim: Delegate side work that would flood the main conversation to a subagent that works in its own context and returns only a summary.
findings.quote: Use one when a side task would flood your main conversation with search results, logs, or file contents you won't reference again: the subagent does that work in its own context and returns only the summary.
findings.title: Create custom subagents

findings.sub_question: What proven patterns keep orchestrator main agent context window low in multi-agent LLM pipelines?
findings.claim: Keep one manager agent owning the final answer while specialist agents handle bounded subtasks via tools or handoffs.
findings.quote: A manager agent keeps control of the conversation and calls specialist agents through Agent.as_tool().
findings.title: Agent orchestration - OpenAI Agents SDK

findings.sub_question: How do ephemeral spawn-delegate-die subagents work in Claude Code OpenCode and similar harnesses?
findings.claim: Claude Code runs each subagent in its own context window and delegates matching tasks to it, which works independently and returns only results.
findings.quote: When Claude encounters a task that matches a subagent’s description, it delegates to that subagent, which works independently and returns results.
findings.title: Create custom subagents - Claude Code Docs

findings.sub_question: How do ephemeral spawn-delegate-die subagents work in Claude Code OpenCode and similar harnesses?
findings.claim: OpenCode lets primary agents automatically invoke subagents for specialized tasks, or users manually invoke them with @ mentions.
findings.quote: Subagents are specialized assistants that primary agents can invoke for specific tasks.
findings.title: Agents | OpenCode

findings.sub_question: What are best practices for splitting large prompt files into lean orchestrator prompts plus detailed worker prompts?
findings.claim: Keep the orchestrator prompt lean by making it own only planning, delegation-prompt writing, dispatch, and result evaluation while workers do all execution work.
findings.quote: It reads the task, decides how to decompose it, writes the delegation prompts, dispatches workers, evaluates what comes back, and decides whether to iterate, escalate, or finish.
findings.title: The Orchestrator-Worker Pattern for AI Coding Agents

findings.sub_question: What are best practices for splitting large prompt files into lean orchestrator prompts plus detailed worker prompts?
findings.claim: Give each worker prompt only three things: a task-scoped system prompt, the minimum necessary context, and a strict expected output format.
findings.quote: The orchestrator creates a subagent with three things: a system prompt scoped to the specific task, the minimum necessary context, and an expected output format.
findings.title: The Orchestrator Pattern (Agent) — Prompt Engines Lab

findings.sub_question: What are best practices for splitting large prompt files into lean orchestrator prompts plus detailed worker prompts?
findings.claim: Isolate each worker with its own clean context, prompt, tool subset, and scratch space so workers do not pollute each other or the orchestrator.
findings.quote: Justified where each sub-task benefits from a clean context (its own prompt, tool subset, and scratch space) so workers do not pollute each other or the orchestrator.
findings.title: Orchestrator-Workers | detached-node

findings.sub_question: How to enforce disjoint file ownership and safe integration when parallel subagents edit code?
findings.claim: Supervise isolated subagents with context quarantine so workers share no state and the main agent integrates only final results.
findings.quote: Subagents isolate this detailed work—the main agent receives only the final result, not the dozens of tool calls that produced it.
findings.title: Subagents - Docs by LangChain

findings.sub_question: How to enforce disjoint file ownership and safe integration when parallel subagents edit code?
findings.claim: Decompose parallel work into focused stateless subtasks owned by independent subagents and merge their returned summaries centrally.
findings.quote: A subagent is an independent AI agent that performs focused work, such as researching a topic, analyzing code, or reviewing changes, and reports the results back to the main agent.
findings.title: Use subagents in Visual Studio Code

findings.sub_question: What verification patterns avoid repeated full test coverage gates while keeping per-file guarantees?
findings.claim: Gate pull requests on diff and patch coverage instead of re-running full project coverage gates.
findings.quote: By default, Codecov will gate and report on coverage changes on Git diff in the Pull request; with overall project coverage reporting available on the Codecov dashboard.
findings.title: Quick Start

findings.sub_question: What verification patterns avoid repeated full test coverage gates while keeping per-file guarantees?
findings.claim: Use --changedSince to run only tests related to changes since a branch or commit.
findings.quote: Runs tests related to the changes since the provided branch or commit hash.
findings.title: Jest CLI Options · Jest

findings.sub_question: What verification patterns avoid repeated full test coverage gates while keeping per-file guarantees?
findings.claim: Use affected commands to run tasks only on projects impacted by a pull request instead of re-testing everything.
findings.quote: As your workspace grows, re-testing, re-building, and re-linting all projects becomes too slow.
findings.title: Run Only Tasks Affected by a PR | Nx
